title: Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment SF 2025
subtitle: It is happening. Get your tickets now
body_html:
Last year, my friend Grady Hannah gave me a call. He said we needed to do a “Live” version of my newsletter. This seemed like a delightfully silly idea, and a series of conferences was born: RAMHT. After going back and forth on the pronunciation of the acronym (It’s pronounced like “ramp-t” not “ram-it”), we had two sold-out events in 2024—the first held at J.P. Morgan Health (“JPM”) and the second during the American Psychiatric Association Annual Meeting.

This year, we kick off the night before the JPM conference on January 12th. The next event is in LA, which coincides with the American Psychiatric Association annual meeting!

Get Your Tickets for RAMHT Here

In the year prior, we had friends debut groundbreaking data on Ibogaine, fMRI-Guided Accelerated TMS (the SAINT branded version, no less), and were joined by Lykos Theraputics before the FDA dashed their dreams of rapid approval…and this year, oh my gosh! We are bringing live demos of things— here and now—the future of rapid-acting mental health diagnostics and treatments.

Videra Health built (among other things) a Tardive Dyskinesia Screening tool. As an investigation of that trial, I can tell you it’s incredible. It’s called TDscreen, and the even more advanced TDetect version is coming soon. You can sign up to use it with your patients now! Yes, it will be on display at the RAMHT SF 2025.

We heard about Sanmai from at last year’s event, when she described transcranial-focused ultrasound for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder. It’s still undergoing clinical trials, but founder Jay Sanguinetti will join us with a demo of what it looks like to stimulate the brain with ultrasound.

GrayMatters Health has broken new ground this year with PRISM — Amygdala-derived-EEG-fMRI-pattern neurofeedback for the treatment of chronic post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). It’s FDA-cleared treatment for PTSD—like therapy you don’t have to talk about. It’s also a video game you play with your brain.

While clinicians evaluate their patients, they no longer need to be distracted with endless notes, thanks to MDhub.ai, which I use for all my clinical work and who will join us for a real-time demo of their technology.

Let's not forget Nightwear—an AI-guided digital therapeutic for the treatment of nightmare disorder, particularly in those with PTSD. Grady, the co-host of this event, is also a co-founder of that company. Treatments and diagnostics that work fast are what it’s all about.

We will have panelists discussing all this and more— and invite plenty of time for our audience to hang out with the panelists. Let’s build the future together.

Share
